findings.title: JSONL writes repeatedly invalidate active development updates
findings.why_it_matters: The documented --diagnostics-file ./diagnostics.jsonl places diagnostics inside the recursively watched project. Every delivered event then invalidates development: an isolated RPC causes unnecessary project preparation, and events arriving faster than the default 75ms debounce continually postpone a saved source update or abort one already running. Excluding the owned output path from source invalidation preserves native development behavior while retaining cwd-relative output.
findings.validation_reason: The diff adds the CLI file sink at apps/loom/src/cli.ts:361-371 without passing its path through commands/dev.ts:32-33, so the documented in-project diagnostics.jsonl writes from diagnostics/output.ts:38 reach dev/watcher.ts:20-30 and repeatedly abort/reset the 75 ms coordinator at dev/coordinator.ts:87-93, causing preparation for isolated writes and postponing source updates when delivered writes remain less than 75 ms apart; the CLI caller establishes reachability, but runtime incidence was not measured under source-only authority.

findings.suggested_fix: Remove the new disable directives and refactor the affected boundary code to satisfy the enabled rules while preserving own-descriptor projection. Use primitive schema guards as already demonstrated by Schema.is in metrics.ts and otlp.ts, validate descriptor values into a named primitive result before returning them, and type the projection accumulator with its finite primitive value union instead of Record<string, unknown>. Preserve hostile accessor/proxy and cancellation behavior; re-review and run the affected checks when execution is authorized.
findings.title: Remove prohibited anti-slop rule suppressions
findings.why_it_matters: The new decoder disables four anti-slop checks for the entire file, so current and future code in this privacy boundary bypasses checks the project explicitly requires. Additional new inline suppressions in the decoder, session and tests repeat the same standards violation. Passing lint with these directives does not establish compliance with CLAUDE.md's requirement to fix violations instead of suppressing rules.
findings.validation_reason: The newly added apps/loom/src/tooling/diagnostics/project.ts:1 and :122 explicitly suppress bundled anti-slop rules despite CLAUDE.md:3 requiring violations to be fixed instead of suppressed, with additional new suppressions at diagnostics/session.ts:118,127,144; the prohibited directives are present in the reviewed diff, so this standards violation requires no runtime precondition.

findings.suggested_fix: Use controlled timers and abort-aware controlled transport promises to prove the exact shared 2000 ms stop deadline and owner release. Preserve the strict existing two-second contract and assertions, request-count, failure-count, and replacement-session checks. Do not raise elapsed-time thresholds or adopt the cited 2400 ms tolerance. Any execution requires a queued grant.
findings.title: Remove the real-clock race from shared-deadline test
findings.why_it_matters: The real hung collector and 10010 ms sleep leave roughly 10 ms of scheduling margin before the strict 2000 ms stop assertion. Timer dispatch or abort settlement can exhaust that margin even with the shared deadline configured correctly. Use controlled time to prove the exact deadline without relaxing the contract or assertions.
findings.synthesis_note: The real-clock race is retained for validation, but the reviewer proposal to relax the loopback assertion is rejected by the explicit no-relaxed-2sec-contract/assertions constraint. No runtime incidence was measured. The existing 2400 ms assertion is context only, not an approved precedent.
findings.validation_reason: The new diagnostics-telemetry.test.ts:144-160 uses a real hung collector and a 10010 ms sleep before asserting elapsed stop time strictly below 2000 ms, while diagnostics/otlp.ts:83-84,178-180,194-198 serially awaits the periodic request and final request with timer-driven cancellation, allowing scheduling or abort-settlement delay to exhaust the roughly 10 ms nominal margin even with the shared deadline configured correctly; this reachable ordering confirms the deterministic-clock concern without endorsing threshold relaxation, and failure incidence was not measured under source-only authority.
